sites.name: Tokyo Tower
sites.fact: Completed in 1958 and 333 metres tall. It is painted white and international orange for air safety.
sites.hint: The orange and white lattice tower south of the Imperial Palace.

sites.name: Tokyo Skytree
sites.fact: At 634 metres, the tallest tower in the world. It opened in 2012.
sites.hint: The very tall pale tower east of the Sumida River.

sites.name: Imperial Palace
sites.fact: The home of the Emperor, on the site of Edo Castle. The castle's moats and stone walls remain.
sites.hint: The green island of trees and moats in the middle of the city.

sites.name: Shibuya Crossing
sites.fact: Often called the busiest pedestrian crossing in the world. Traffic stops in every direction at once and people cross all ways.
sites.hint: Outside Shibuya Station, in the west of the city.

sites.name: Sensō-ji
sites.fact: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 645 according to tradition. A giant red lantern hangs in its Thunder Gate.
sites.hint: In Asakusa, near the Sumida River, a little west of the Skytree.

sites.name: Tokyo Station
sites.fact: The red-brick station building opened in 1914. Shinkansen bullet trains leave from here.
sites.hint: Just east of the Imperial Palace gardens.

sites.name: Shinjuku
sites.fact: The twin-towered Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building opened in 1991. Shinjuku Station nearby is the busiest railway station in the world.
sites.hint: The cluster of skyscrapers in the west, north of Shibuya.

sites.name: Rainbow Bridge
sites.fact: A suspension bridge across the northern part of Tokyo Bay, opened in 1993. It links the city to the man-made island of Odaiba.
sites.hint: The white suspension bridge over the harbour, south of Tokyo Tower.

sites.name: Meiji Shrine
sites.fact: A Shinto shrine to Emperor Meiji, completed in 1920. The forest around it was planted with about 100,000 donated trees.
sites.hint: The dense forest between Shibuya and Shinjuku.

sites.name: Haneda Airport
sites.fact: Tokyo's main domestic airport and one of the busiest in the world, built on reclaimed land at the edge of the bay.
sites.hint: On the bay shore, well south of the city centre.

sites.name: Ueno Park
sites.fact: One of Japan's first public parks, established in 1873. It is known for its museums and its cherry blossom.
sites.hint: The park with a pond, north-east of the Imperial Palace.

sites.name: Tokyo Dome
sites.fact: A stadium opened in 1988, home of the Yomiuri Giants baseball team. Its white roof is held up by air pressure.
sites.hint: The white dome north of the Imperial Palace.
